chapter_theme: Truth (வாய்மை), taken as the true as against the false in the whole person: the Lord mingles with those who are mingled with truth and does not enter before the false; knowledge without the all-knowing is no gain; those who leave falsehood and the bewildering senses and follow the one who cut away confusion reach the Siva-state.
structure_note: 2600, 2601 and 2604 repeat one formula (மெய்கலந்தாரொடு மெய்கலந்தான், பொய்கலந்தார் முன் புகுதா) with variations; around them are verses on grace, on knowledge, and on cutting the senses' hold (2603, 2607, 2608).

2595.reading: Put plainly, the teachings of grace are like gold refined of its flaw in fire: if one holds to them until all is cut away, without the least loss of fineness, one becomes a bright flame with enmity cut off.
2595.nuance: மாற்று is the fineness of gold as tested on the touchstone, so இறை மாற்று அற is read as 'without the slightest loss of fineness'; it might instead mean 'with the Lord's change' or 'with no exchange'. அற்றது உரைக்கில் may mean 'if one speaks of what is detached'.

2596.reading: Leaving aside the knowledge that knows everything, even knowing everything there is no gain; if I say that the knowledge that knows everything is 'I', it can be called the all-knowing Lord.
2596.nuance: எல்லாம் opens every line. Lines 1 and 2 are clear: all knowledge apart from the all-knowing is fruitless. Lines 3 and 4 may say that one who takes that knowledge as oneself is one with the Lord, or warn against claiming it; I read the first, in keeping with the neighbouring chapters on 'that you are'.

2597.reading: Doing tapas on the high mountain, I too passed beyond the base, wretched cycle of birth and found the form known to the goddess, the thief who stands in the kalas.
2597.nuance: முலைநின்ற மாது is taken as Uma, and கலைநின்ற கள்வன் (the thief who stands in the kalas) as Siva, hidden in the phases of the moon or of the breath, or in the arts. கள்வன் for the Lord who steals the heart is an old devotional usage.

2598.reading: He alone is fit to be called lord in the world; he alone stands as the principle of the world; as the sky pours rain, the great Veda abounds; and the heart whose flesh has melted becomes one with him.
2598.nuance: Line 3 is compressed: வானே மழைபொழி மாமறை கூர்ந்திடும் may compare the Lord's gift of the Veda to rain, or name him as sky, rain and Veda. ஊனே உருகிய உள்ளம் (a heart melted to the flesh) is the language of devotional love.

2599.reading: What is the cause of their gaining grace? It is that, with minds free of darkness, they seek the Lord, change their deluded minds, and praise the red feet that hold the rare substance.
2599.nuance: The verse answers its own question. அமரில் in line 1 is unclear: it may mean 'in desire', 'among the gods' or 'in the struggle'.

2600.reading: The one who mingles in truth with those who mingle in truth and does not enter before those mingled with falsehood stands as the saving Lord of the ages, and for the true, joy grows from mingling in truth.
2600.nuance: மெய் means truth and also the body, so மெய்கலந்தார் can be those joined in truth or those in whom the Lord has entered bodily; the chapter title favours truth. The Lord's presence follows the person's truthfulness: he goes in where there is truth and not where there is falsehood.

2601.reading: The pure one who mingles in truth with those who mingle in truth and does not go in among those mingled with falsehood: only those who have joined hands with him can fix that Lord in their thought when the breath rises to leave.
2601.nuance: ஆவி எழும்பொழுது (when the breath rises) is taken as the moment of death, when only those already joined to the Lord can hold him in mind. கைகலந்தார் (those who joined hands) may also mean those who joined him in worship with folded hands.

2602.reading: If, when the time comes, one performs Siva's truth at both times of day, it stands as the higher rule; if one gives up falsehood and the senses as refuge, the Lord himself becomes that way.
2602.nuance: இருபொழுதும் (both times) is taken as morning and evening worship. மெய்செயின் may be 'do truth' or 'do Siva's worship with the body'; புகல் ஒன்று நீத்திடில் is read as giving up the refuge one takes in falsehood and the senses.

2603.reading: What comes and what fails to come: this is grace; the excellent, glorious Nandi gave grace so that one may be saved; if one masters the nine paths of the lying senses, one can mount the horse called truth.
2603.nuance: நெறி ஒன்பது (nine paths) may be the nine openings of the body; புரவி (horse) is the vehicle of ascent. மெய் என் புரவி may mean 'the horse called truth' or 'the horse called the body'; both suit Tirumular.

2604.reading: The one who joined hands with me, Nandi in my thought, the one who mingled in truth, the first of the Veda, the pure one who does not enter before the false, is a refuge only to those who have cast off falsehood.
2604.nuance: The verse gathers the chapter's epithets and ends where 2600 and 2601 point: the Lord is refuge (புகலிடம்) to those who have left falsehood, not to all.

2605.reading: No one knows how to open, with their own hand, the bolt of Nandi who dwells in the inner shrine of the true feet; if you put away the false bolt of suffering so that falsehood ends, the opening of the bolt is the rare gain.
2605.nuance: தாள் means both foot and door-bolt, and the verse plays on both: மெய்த்தாள் (true feet, or true bolt), கைத்தாள் (hand-bolt), பொய்த்தாள் (false bolt), கத்தாள் (perhaps a corruption). The Lord is pictured behind a locked inner door that effort cannot open but the ending of falsehood can.

2606.reading: Praise him in your awareness, in the way that saves; the true path of Hara stands firm above; in the midst of those who shine without any falsehood, the Lord sits and stands.
2606.nuance: புறம் பொலிவார் (those who shine outward) suggests people whose outward life shows their inner truth; the Lord's seat is among them.

2607.reading: There is a fruit of the fragrant flower; he does not let the bird that comes to it enter and eat; if you shoot an arrow and drive the bird far away, you can reach the red-gold Siva-state.
2607.nuance: The image is symbolic and not explained. The fruit may be the bliss or nectar of yoga, and the bird the senses or the ego that would consume it; the arrow, as in 2567, the aimed mind. Who 'he' is in line 2 is unclear.

2608.reading: Cut the bond of the five bewildering senses and follow the one who cut away confusion; when I followed, Siva our Lord, without wavering, made my mind one, saying 'go and be saved'.
2608.nuance: ஐம்புலப் பாசம் names the senses as a பாசம், a bond in the Siddhanta sense. துயக்கறுத்தான் (the one who cut away confusion) may be the guru or Siva himself; the verse moves from the first to the second.

2609.reading: For those who can think with the mind alone, if they do what is fitting toward the Lord in solitude, the body called a heavy burden becomes the act of the pure one, knowledge for the world.
2609.nuance: Lines 2 and 3 (கினமெனக் கூறு மிருங்காய மேவற் றனிவினி) are obscure and the word division is uncertain; இருங்காயம் (the great body) and தனி (alone) are the clearest words. The reading is a guess.

links.note: The Kural says one who is not false in his heart dwells in the hearts of all people; Tirumular says the Lord dwells with those mingled in truth and does not enter before the false. Truthfulness opens the heart in both: to others in the Kural, to the Lord in Tirumular.
The Kural says knowledge from the five senses is no gain without true perception; Tirumular says knowing everything is no gain apart from the knowledge that knows everything.

Both deny that knowledge profits by itself: the Kural asks what learning gains without worship of the one of pure knowledge, Tirumular says knowing all things gains nothing apart from the all-knowing.

Both make the way out of bondage a following: the Kural says cling to the one without clinging in order to let clinging go, Tirumular says cut the senses' bond and follow the one who cut away confusion.
The Kural praises those who keep to the path of the one who quenched the five senses; Tirumular tells the seeker to cut the five senses' bond and follow the one who has done so.

source_issues: 2609: lines 2 and 3 (கினமெனக் கூறு மிருங்காய மேவற் றனிவினி னாதன்பால்) are obscure and possibly corrupt.
2605: கத்தாள் in line 4 is unclear and may be corrupt for கைத்தாள்.
2604: line 4 lacks the closing full stop the other verses have; no change in sense.
